chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn Ziyād, from Kurdawayh al-Hamadanī, who said:
I asked al-ʿAbd al-Ṣāliḥ عليه السلام about the witr, and he said: Join it.

So the proper way regarding all of these narrations is that we carry them upon a form of taqiyyah, because they agree with the doctrines of many of the ʿammah, while the purport of two hadiths among them is choice, and that is not the doctrine of anyone. For whoever deems joining obligatory does not permit separation, and whoever deems separation obligatory does not permit joining. And it is possible that his statement, 'if he wishes he gives salām, and if he wishes he does not give salām,' is an indication toward the speech which becomes permissible by the taslīm, because that is not a condition in it, clarifying what we have mentioned.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precautionary conformity in expression due to circumstances
key_terms.الْفَصْلَ: separating the prayer units from one another
key_terms.الْوَتْرِ: the witr prayer in the night salat
key_terms.بِالتَّسْلِيمِ: by the taslīm; through the salutation concluding salat
key_terms.سَلَّمَ: he gave the taslīm ending the prayer formally
key_terms.صِلْهُ: join it; connect it to what precedes it in prayer form

ai.seo_question: How should Shia hadiths about joining or separating al-shafʿ and al-witr be understood?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling of joining or separating the rakʿatayn of al-shafʿ and al-witr in the night prayer. The passage explains that certain narrations are to be understood as taqiyyah because they align with non-Imami positions, and it clarifies that the issue is a legal one concerning the form of salat and the role of taslīm.
